In the [Password Security](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md) section, there is no mention of complexity or repeated characters. Therefore 111111111111 is a valid password which follows these rules. This does however, not seem like a secure password.

We already have user info & context matching in our application, checking against the top breached passwords was pointless since we have a min. length of 12, and hardly any password in that list was left after filtering on that length.

So this is a genuine question, is 111111111111 therefore considered a secure password? Or any repeated character for that matter, considering you meet the minimum length requirements, since there is absolutely no requirement on complexity?

comments.body:
Hi there, this question is easy to come if to watch one requirement out of context and not the full set of related requirements.

My questions before any further answers:
* are you familiar with https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html ?
* if we measure "secure password" - then secure against what attack vector?
* what risk level (1, 2, 3) of application we are talking about?

Most likely you can find answers to your question from this issue: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1540
I hadn't found that issue when searching, so thank you for linking it. That does answer my question, thank you.

@LiamDobbelaere - note that I opened a separate issue #2747 to address 

> ... checking against the top breached passwords was pointless since we have a min. length of 12, and hardly any password in that list was left after filtering on that length.

title: 111111111111 is a secure password?
